quarterly_data.quarter: Fujifilm press release: Fujifilm to Expand CMP Slurry Production Capacity in the (10-14-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: FUJIFILM Corporation will invest a total of $18 million USD (approximately JPY 3 billion) at the FUJIFILM Electronic Materials U.S.A. production site in Mesa, Arizona to expand capacity for copper interconnect CMP slurries used in BEOL processes and to establish new production facilities capable of multi-product manufacturing of CMP slurries for FEOL, MOL and advanced packaging applications, including hybrid bonding; the new facilities are to bridge product development at the Arizona site's global CMP slurry R&D center and mass production. The expanded production line is scheduled to begin operations in 2027. The company says demand for copper interconnect CMP slurry, a product for which it claims a leading global market share, is increasing in advanced logic and memory, and that major semiconductor manufacturers continue to invest in new and expanded production facilities in the United States. Brian O'Donnelly (president & CEO, FUJIFILM Electronic Materials U.S.A.): 'The advanced semiconductor market has entered a period of significant growth, driven by the rapid expansion of demand related to artificial intelligence.'
quarterly_data.figure: $18 million USD (approximately JPY 3 billion) Mesa, Arizona CMP slurry expansion; operations scheduled to begin in 2027
